value.description: The value to set. For checkboxes use boolean, for selects use option value or text, for other inputs use appropriate string/number

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this form fill does on the page and to what, for example 'Sets the delivery date to 29 September'. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__get_page_text

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m -q --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Disposable upgrade proof: migrate to 0089, seed via the concurrency suite, snapshot, apply 0090, snapshot, re-run suite.
set -uo pipefail
export MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1
S=/d/Hermes/temp/claude/9a7828623b7d9c29/51f19cc3-0f59-4848-a0f1-0d021c85c168/scratchpad
W=/d/tmp/b0-verify
DB=ss_expansion_hardening_races
H=127.0.0.1:55440
log(){ echo "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] $*"; }
docker exec b0-verify-pg psql -U scalesmiths_ci -d ss_expansion_test -qc "CREATE DATABASE $DB" || exit 1
export REDACTED
export MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL=REDACTED
export ADMIN_DATABASE_URL=REDACTED
export WEB_DATABASE_URL=REDACTED
export EXPANSION_TEST_DATABASE_URL=$ADMIN_DATABASE_URL EXPANSION_WEB_TEST_DATABASE_URL=$WEB_DATABASE_URL NO_COLOR=1
cd $W
node -e '
const fs=require("fs");const j=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync("admin/drizzle/meta/_journal.json"));j.entries=j.entries.filter(e=>e.idx!==90);fs.writeFileSync("admin/drizzle/meta/_journal.json",JSON.stringify(j,null,2));
const p=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync("scripts/shared-migration-plan.json"));p.order[p.order.length-1].through=89;fs.writeFileSync("scripts/shared-migration-plan.json",JSON.stringify(p,null,2));'
cd admin
log "stage 1: migrate to 0089"
node scripts/provision-postgres-roles.mjs --confirm-provision | tail -1
node scripts/migrate-shared-test-database.mjs | tail -1
node scripts/provision-postgres-roles.mjs --confirm-provision | tail -1
node scripts/verify-postgres-privileges.mjs | tail -2
log "stage 2: seed with suite on 0089"
npx vitest run --config vitest.integration.config.ts test/integration/expansion-concurrency.integration.test.ts --testTimeout 300000 --hookTimeout 300000 < /dev/null > $S/u-seed.log 2>&1
grep -E '^ +Tests +' $S/u-seed.log
docker exec b0-verify-pg psql -U scalesmiths_ci -d $DB -Atq -f /snapshot.sql > $S/u-before.txt
log "before snapshot: $(wc -l < $S/u-before.txt) tables"
cd $W && git -c core.autocrlf=false checkout HEAD -- admin/drizzle/meta/_journal.json scripts/shared-migration-plan.json && cd admin
log "stage 3: apply 0090"
node scripts/migrate-shared-test-database.mjs | tail -2
node scripts/provision-postgres-roles.mjs --confirm-provision | tail -1
node scripts/verify-postgres-privileges.mjs | tail -2
docker exec b0-verify-pg psql -U scalesmiths_ci -d $DB -Atq -f /snapshot.sql > $S/u-after.txt
log "after snapshot: $(wc -l < $S/u-after.txt) tables; diff:"
diff $S/u-before.txt $S/u-after.txt
docker exec b0-verify-pg psql -U scalesmiths_ci -d $DB -At -f /checks.sql 2>&1 | grep -E 'trigger:|released rows|ERROR'
log "stage 4: suite on upgraded schema"
npx vitest run --config vitest.integration.config.ts test/integration/expansion-concurrency.integration.test.ts --testTimeout 300000 --hookTimeout 300000 < /dev/null > $S/u-post.log 2>&1
grep -E '^ +Tests +|×' $S/u-post.log | cut -c1-200
log "done"

# B0 merge readiness

Status: **NOT MERGED. Blocked on governance: no eligible human code-owner reviewer exists, and GitHub does not enforce the documented branch protection on `master`.** Engineering verification is complete.

Verified 2026-11-20 by an agent. Model review is not human approval and has not been presented as one.

## State

| Item | Observed |
|---|---|
| PR | #155, draft, open, `claude/modest-newton-jo2d95` -> `master` |
| PR head | `173714ed52a279856b3c7c59de6516ce6fd9187f` (only change since the last fully green head `a82a605` is this document) |
| Master | `4c399b87e833b12d15791f6b5f8b08ab35871667` (merge of #154); merge base equals master, branch is 0 behind / 41 ahead |
| Reviews | none; no review requests; 0 review threads, 0 unresolved |
| Mergeable | `MERGEABLE` |

## CI on the final head

Workflows triggered by `pull_request` on `173714e`: CI run 44719629619, Security 44719629455, CodeQL 44719629730. All 21 required check contexts in `scripts/branch-protection-policy.json` now report `success`.

Cross-browser Smoke was cancelled on the first attempt: the job sat in `npx playwright install --with-deps firefox webkit` until the job timeout (25 min) and the runner killed it. No test ran. The commit only changed this document, and the same job passed on `a82a605`. The failed job was re-run once without changes and passed (attempt 2, started 11:29 UTC). Diagnosis: transient runner/package-mirror stall, not a code defect.

## Migration 0090

| Check | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Sequence | `0090_expansion_domain_release_guard_hardening` is journal idx 90, `when` strictly after 0089; the shared plan's last admin range runs through 90 | `admin/drizzle/meta/_journal.json`, `scripts/shared-migration-plan.json` |
| Checksum | committed blob sha256 `b9a0dbb7…c1c9` matches `scripts/migration-checksums.json` | `git show HEAD:<file> \| sha256sum` |
| Repository gates | `check-migrations`, `check-shared-migration-plan` (115 migrations), `check-migration-history` (52 historical + 63 forward locked) pass locally; the same gates pass in CI | local run, CI `Database and Migrations` |
| Fresh database | CI applies 0090 on every integration database and on the dedicated `postgres-expansion` service, then the restricted-role privilege verifier passes | CI job log (run 44717578398 on `a82a605`, identical migrations) |
| Concurrency on the migrated schema | 89/89, 0 skipped, run as `scalesmiths_expansion_admin` / `scalesmiths_expansion_web` after 0090 was applied; the step fails on any skipped test | same job log |
| Upgrade from a checkpoint-5 (0089) database with history | UPGRADE_RESULT | isolated `postgres:16` container, see below |
| Guard behaviour after upgrade | INSERT of a released row refused (new in 0090); rewriting or clearing a recorded release refused; direct release of a non-withdrawn prospect refused; release without a reason refused | `checks-0090.sql` against the upgraded database |
| Founder-controlled release | founder-only, reason required, idempotent replay, audited `domain_released` event, permanent history, suppression still applies; a partner is refused | concurrency test "a founder can release the domain held by an excluded, released candidate" |
| Restricted principals | `verify-postgres-privileges.mjs` passes before and after 0090 on the isolated database, and in CI | local and CI logs |

The supplied `database-migration-logs.zip` ended at `admin/0089`; it was not used as evidence for 0090.

Isolated upgrade method: a detached worktree at `173714e`; a disposable `postgres:16` container; shared migrator run with 0090 temporarily removed from the journal and plan (worktree only, restored afterwards, never committed); history seeded by running the concurrency suite on the 0089 schema; a per-table row count and content digest of every `expansion_*` table taken; 0090 applied by the normal migrator; the digest repeated and compared; the concurrency suite re-run on the upgraded schema.

## Remediation review

| Finding | Status on the final head |
|---|---|
| Geographic exclusivity | Fixed in 0088: founder-approved `expansion_areas` tree; containment comes from the tree, not wording; unclassified wording goes to review (fail-closed). Covered by the 5B geography test. |
| Public profile entitlement | Fixed in 0089: the security-barrier view requires a live webpage reward, a current qualified-client count at or above its milestone, and no open qualification flag. Suspension is automatic on the next request; records are kept; a founder restoring entitlement restores the page. Covered by the 5E tests. |
| Released-candidate domain lock | Fixed in 0088 + 0090: founder-only, audited, permanent release for a withdrawn, unworked prospect from an excluded candidate; 0090 makes the database guard match the owner guard and cover INSERT. |
| Concurrency suite in CI | Fixed: `ci.yml` adds a `postgres-expansion` service and two steps; runs as restricted roles; fails if any test is skipped. |

No critical or high findings remain from the agent review. One low-severity test-portability issue: two tests (`expansion-concurrency.integration.test.ts:686`, `expansion-finance.test.ts:315`) select `amount_pence::text` and `ORDER BY amount_pence`, which sorts the text output column. It passes on CI's `postgres:16-alpine` and failed once on a Debian `postgres:16` (`en_US.utf8`) because that collation ignores the minus sign. No production query uses the pattern. Recommended follow-up, not a B0 blocker.

All protected flags default off and are checked with `=== "true"`: `PARTNER_APPLICATIONS_ENABLED`, `PARTNER_ACTIVATION_ENABLED`, `PARTNER_PROFILE_PUBLICATION_ENABLED`, `PUBLIC_PARTNER_PROFILES_ENABLED`, `PARTNER_RETENTION_EXECUTION_ENABLED`. Withdrawals additionally need a founder-enabled commercial plan.

## Deployment impact of merging

Merging runs CI, Security and CodeQL on `master` (push trigger). No workflow deploys, uses an environment, or connects to a server; the repository has no deployment environments or webhooks. Production deployment is a separate, manual release-manager operation (`docs/operations/release-runbook.md`). Not verified: any host-side automation outside GitHub (for example a scheduled pull on the VPS).

## Blockers

1. **No eligible human code-owner reviewer.** `.github/CODEOWNERS` assigns every path to `@TheFridey`, the PR author and the repository's only collaborator. GitHub does not allow an author to approve their own PR, so the required code-owner approval cannot be given by anyone.
2. **Branch protection is documented but not applied.** `GET /repos/TheFridey/ScaleSmiths/branches/master/protection` returns `404 Branch not protected`, and the repository has no rulesets. `scripts/branch-protection-policy.json` (1 approval, code-owner review, last-push approval, conversation resolution, up-to-date branch, 20 required checks) is therefore not enforced. A merge would technically succeed today; that is exactly why it was not attempted.
3. PR is still a draft.

## Proposed resolution (repository owner only)

The agent has not changed repository settings and will not.

1. Add a trusted second person as a collaborator with write access, and list them in `CODEOWNERS` for the protected paths (at least `admin/drizzle/`, `.github/`, the restricted-role scripts and the Expansion server code).
2. Apply `scripts/branch-protection-policy.json` to `master` (classic protection or a ruleset), and confirm `check-branch-protection-policy.mjs` reports no drift.
3. That reviewer reviews against the checklist below and approves after the final push.
4. Owner marks the PR ready, confirms deployment impact, and merges.

If the owner instead chooses a documented solo-maintainer exception, that is the owner's decision, should be recorded in `docs/operations/protected-areas-and-branch-protection.md`, and still does not make an agent or model review count as approval.

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] **Migrations 0073-0090**: forward-only, none rewritten, journal/plan/checksums agree; 0088 area tree and domain release columns; 0089 view; 0090 guard (INSERT path, permanent history). Rollback is restore-from-backup, not down-migrations.
- [ ] **Financial invariants**: commission is never paid from conditional rewards; refunds adjust unpaid or reserved commission; negative adjustments travel with withdrawals; no double allocation under contention; ledger and audit append-only.
- [ ] **PostgreSQL privileges**: web role reads only the security-barrier view; admin runtime role cannot migrate or own schema; `provision-postgres-roles.mjs` and `verify-postgres-privileges.mjs` agree.
- [ ] **Public profile view**: only live, consented, approved content of an active partner with current entitlement; no private columns; partner self-takedown.
- [ ] **Exclusivity**: area-tree containment, fail-closed review for unclassified wording, partner requests never evaluated against exclusivity.
- [ ] **Domain allocation and release**: single holder under races; release founder-only, reasoned, audited, permanent; suppression unaffected.
- [ ] **CI workflow**: `postgres-expansion` service, CI-only credentials, skip guard; no new secrets, permissions or deploy steps.
- [ ] **Production deployment triggers**: none in GitHub; confirm no host-side automation.
- [ ] **Rollback**: restore the pre-migration backup; keep all partner flags unset.

## After a permitted merge

Verify the merge commit and its tree on `master`, inspect `master` CI, confirm every protected flag above remains unset in production configuration, and confirm no deployment occurred. Do not activate partner intake, public profiles, withdrawals or rewards. B1 (Operation Empower) must not begin until this is recorded.

# B0 merge readiness

Status: **NOT MERGED. Blocked on governance: no eligible human code-owner reviewer exists, and GitHub does not enforce the documented branch protection on `master`.** Engineering verification is complete.

Verified 2026-11-20 by an agent. Model review is not human approval and has not been presented as one.

## State

| Item | Observed |
|---|---|
| PR | #155, draft, open, `claude/modest-newton-jo2d95` -> `master` |
| PR head | `173714ed52a279856b3c7c59de6516ce6fd9187f` (only change since the last fully green head `a82a605` is this document) |
| Master | `4c399b87e833b12d15791f6b5f8b08ab35871667` (merge of #154); merge base equals master, branch is 0 behind / 41 ahead |
| Reviews | none; no review requests; 0 review threads, 0 unresolved |
| Mergeable | `MERGEABLE` |

## CI on the final head

Workflows triggered by `pull_request` on `173714e`: CI run 44719629619, Security 44719629455, CodeQL 44719629730. All 21 required check contexts in `scripts/branch-protection-policy.json` now report `success`.

Cross-browser Smoke was cancelled on the first attempt: the job sat in `npx playwright install --with-deps firefox webkit` until the job timeout (25 min) and the runner killed it. No test ran. The commit only changed this document, and the same job passed on `a82a605`. The failed job was re-run once without changes and passed (attempt 2, started 11:29 UTC). Diagnosis: transient runner/package-mirror stall, not a code defect.

## Migration 0090

| Check | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Sequence | `0090_expansion_domain_release_guard_hardening` is journal idx 90, `when` strictly after 0089; the shared plan's last admin range runs through 90 | `admin/drizzle/meta/_journal.json`, `scripts/shared-migration-plan.json` |
| Checksum | committed blob sha256 `b9a0dbb7…c1c9` matches `scripts/migration-checksums.json` | `git show HEAD:<file> \| sha256sum` |
| Repository gates | `check-migrations`, `check-shared-migration-plan` (115 migrations), `check-migration-history` (52 historical + 63 forward locked) pass locally; the same gates pass in CI | local run, CI `Database and Migrations` |
| Fresh database | CI applies 0090 on every integration database and on the dedicated `postgres-expansion` service, then the restricted-role privilege verifier passes | CI job log (run 44717578398 on `a82a605`, identical migrations) |
| Concurrency on the migrated schema | 89/89, 0 skipped, run as `scalesmiths_expansion_admin` / `scalesmiths_expansion_web` after 0090 was applied; the step fails on any skipped test | same job log |
| Upgrade from a checkpoint-5 (0089) database with history | UPGRADE_RESULT | isolated `postgres:16` container, see below |
| Guard behaviour after upgrade | INSERT of a released row refused (new in 0090); rewriting or clearing a recorded release refused; direct release of a non-withdrawn prospect refused; release without a reason refused | `checks-0090.sql` against the upgraded database |
| Founder-controlled release | founder-only, reason required, idempotent replay, audited `domain_released` event, permanent history, suppression still applies; a partner is refused | concurrency test "a founder can release the domain held by an excluded, released candidate" |
| Restricted principals | `verify-postgres-privileges.mjs` passes before and after 0090 on the isolated database, and in CI | local and CI logs |

The supplied `database-migration-logs.zip` ended at `admin/0089`; it was not used as evidence for 0090.

Isolated upgrade method: a detached worktree at `173714e`; a disposable `postgres:16` container; shared migrator run with 0090 temporarily removed from the journal and plan (worktree only, restored afterwards, never committed); history seeded by running the concurrency suite on the 0089 schema; a per-table row count and content digest of every `expansion_*` table taken; 0090 applied by the normal migrator; the digest repeated and compared; the concurrency suite re-run on the upgraded schema.

## Remediation review

| Finding | Status on the final head |
|---|---|
| Geographic exclusivity | Fixed in 0088: founder-approved `expansion_areas` tree; containment comes from the tree, not wording; unclassified wording goes to review (fail-closed). Covered by the 5B geography test. |
| Public profile entitlement | Fixed in 0089: the security-barrier view requires a live webpage reward, a current qualified-client count at or above its milestone, and no open qualification flag. Suspension is automatic on the next request; records are kept; a founder restoring entitlement restores the page. Covered by the 5E tests. |
| Released-candidate domain lock | Fixed in 0088 + 0090: founder-only, audited, permanent release for a withdrawn, unworked prospect from an excluded candidate; 0090 makes the database guard match the owner guard and cover INSERT. |
| Concurrency suite in CI | Fixed: `ci.yml` adds a `postgres-expansion` service and two steps; runs as restricted roles; fails if any test is skipped. |

No critical or high findings remain from the agent review. One low-severity test-portability issue: two tests (`expansion-concurrency.integration.test.ts:686`, `expansion-finance.test.ts:315`) select `amount_pence::text` and `ORDER BY amount_pence`, which sorts the text output column. It passes on CI's `postgres:16-alpine` and failed once on a Debian `postgres:16` (`en_US.utf8`) because that collation ignores the minus sign. No production query uses the pattern. Recommended follow-up, not a B0 blocker.

Protected flags default to `false` in `.env.example`. `PARTNER_APPLICATIONS_ENABLED`, `PARTNER_ACTIVATION_ENABLED`, `PARTNER_PROFILE_PUBLICATION_ENABLED` and `PUBLIC_PARTNER_PROFILES_ENABLED` are read with `=== "true"`, so anything else is closed. `PARTNER_RETENTION_EXECUTION_ENABLED` also defaults to `false`; its reader was not inspected in this pass. Withdrawals additionally need a founder-enabled commercial plan.

## Deployment impact of merging

Merging runs CI, Security and CodeQL on `master` (push trigger). No workflow deploys, uses an environment, or connects to a server; the repository has no deployment environments or webhooks. Production deployment is a separate, manual release-manager operation (`docs/operations/release-runbook.md`). Not verified: any host-side automation outside GitHub (for example a scheduled pull on the VPS).

## Blockers

1. **No eligible human code-owner reviewer.** `.github/CODEOWNERS` assigns every path to `@TheFridey`, the PR author and the repository's only collaborator. GitHub does not allow an author to approve their own PR, so the required code-owner approval cannot be given by anyone.
2. **Branch protection is documented but not applied.** `GET /repos/TheFridey/ScaleSmiths/branches/master/protection` returns `404 Branch not protected`, and the repository has no rulesets. `scripts/branch-protection-policy.json` (1 approval, code-owner review, last-push approval, conversation resolution, up-to-date branch, 20 required checks) is therefore not enforced. A merge would technically succeed today; that is exactly why it was not attempted.
3. PR is still a draft.

## Proposed resolution (repository owner only)

The agent has not changed repository settings and will not.

1. Add a trusted second person as a collaborator with write access, and list them in `CODEOWNERS` for the protected paths (at least `admin/drizzle/`, `.github/`, the restricted-role scripts and the Expansion server code).
2. Apply `scripts/branch-protection-policy.json` to `master` (classic protection or a ruleset), and confirm `check-branch-protection-policy.mjs` reports no drift.
3. That reviewer reviews against the checklist below and approves after the final push.
4. Owner marks the PR ready, confirms deployment impact, and merges.

If the owner instead chooses a documented solo-maintainer exception, that is the owner's decision, should be recorded in `docs/operations/protected-areas-and-branch-protection.md`, and still does not make an agent or model review count as approval.

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] **Migrations 0073-0090**: forward-only, none rewritten, journal/plan/checksums agree; 0088 area tree and domain release columns; 0089 view; 0090 guard (INSERT path, permanent history). Rollback is restore-from-backup, not down-migrations.
- [ ] **Financial invariants**: commission is never paid from conditional rewards; refunds adjust unpaid or reserved commission; negative adjustments travel with withdrawals; no double allocation under contention; ledger and audit append-only.
- [ ] **PostgreSQL privileges**: web role reads only the security-barrier view; admin runtime role cannot migrate or own schema; `provision-postgres-roles.mjs` and `verify-postgres-privileges.mjs` agree.
- [ ] **Public profile view**: only live, consented, approved content of an active partner with current entitlement; no private columns; partner self-takedown.
- [ ] **Exclusivity**: area-tree containment, fail-closed review for unclassified wording, partner requests never evaluated against exclusivity.
- [ ] **Domain allocation and release**: single holder under races; release founder-only, reasoned, audited, permanent; suppression unaffected.
- [ ] **CI workflow**: `postgres-expansion` service, CI-only credentials, skip guard; no new secrets, permissions or deploy steps.
- [ ] **Production deployment triggers**: none in GitHub; confirm no host-side automation.
- [ ] **Rollback**: restore the pre-migration backup; keep all partner flags unset.

## After a permitted merge

Verify the merge commit and its tree on `master`, inspect `master` CI, confirm every protected flag above remains unset in production configuration, and confirm no deployment occurred. Do not activate partner intake, public profiles, withdrawals or rewards. B1 (Operation Empower) must not begin until this is recorded.

content.text:
PR #155 is **not merged**. CI is green and migration 0090 checks out, but no human code-owner approval can be given under the current repo setup, so I didn't attempt the merge. | Item | Result | |---|---| | PR head | `173714ed52a279856b3c7c59de6516ce6fd9187f`. The only change since the last fully green head `a82a605` is the readiness doc. | | Master | `4c399b87e833b12d15791f6b5f8b08ab35871667`. It hasn't moved; the branch is 0 behind and 41 ahead. | | CI | All 21 required checks pass on `173714e`. Cross-browser Smoke had been cancelled while installing Playwright browsers, before any test ran. I re-ran it once and it passed. | | Migration 0090 | **Verified.**
  • It is entry 90 in the journal, after 0089.
  • The committed file's checksum matches `migration-checksums.json`, and the three migration integrity checks pass.
  • CI applies it on every fresh database, then the restricted-role privilege check passes and the concurrency suite passes 89/89 with 0 skipped.
  • I upgraded a throwaway 0089 database holding test data: only 0090 was applied, and all 53 `expansion_*` tables kept identical row counts and contents (214 opportunities, 2 with released domains).
  • Privilege checks passed before and after the upgrade.
  • Released-domain rules hold: inserting an already-released row, rewriting a release, releasing a prospect that isn't withdrawn, and releasing without a reason are all refused.
I didn't use the supplied zip as evidence, since it ends at 0089. | | Risk review | All four remediations are present. No critical or high findings remain from my review, which is not a human approval. One low-severity test issue: two tests sort a number converted to text, so the order depends on the database's collation. They pass on CI's PostgreSQL image and failed on my local Debian one. No production code uses the pattern. | | Human review | None. There are no reviews and no review requests. | | Deployment impact | Merging only runs CI, Security and CodeQL on master. No workflow deploys, and the repo has no environments or webhooks. I couldn't check for automation on the server itself, such as a scheduled pull on the VPS. | | Merge status | **Not merged.** | **Blockers**, which only you as repo owner can fix: 1. **No one can give the code-owner approval.** `CODEOWNERS` assigns every path to `@TheFridey`, who is the PR author and the only collaborator, and GitHub doesn't let an author approve their own PR. So I couldn't request an independent reviewer: there is nobody eligible. 2. **Master isn't protected.** The GitHub API returns "Branch not protected" and the repo has no rulesets, so the rules in `scripts/branch-protection-policy.json` aren't enforced. A merge would technically go through today, which is why I didn't try one. 3. The PR is still a draft. **Proposed fix:** add a trusted second collaborator and make them a code owner for the protected paths. Then apply `branch-protection-policy.json` to master and have that person review against the checklist in the doc. If you'd rather work solo, that's a decision to record in the protected-areas doc; it still wouldn't make a model review count as approval. **Deliverable:** I updated `docs/expansion/intelligence/B0-MERGE-READINESS.md` with the evidence, blockers, reviewer checklist and post-merge steps. It's committed as `586f777` on a local branch `b0-readiness-update` in the worktree `D:\tmp\b0-verify`, and not pushed. I've also drafted a corrected PR description: the current one still lists the four findings as open, says CI doesn't run the concurrency suite, and only covers migrations to 0087. Pushing the commit starts a new CI run on a new head. I removed the throwaway PostgreSQL container. B1 has not been started.
